first: भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
en: Krishna said: Listen again, strong-armed one, to my highest teaching. You are dear to me, so I will tell it to you for your good.

first: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः ।
en: Neither the crowds of gods nor the great sages know where I come from. For I am the source of the gods and of the great sages in every way.
Whoever knows me as unborn, without beginning, and the great Lord of the worlds is free of confusion among mortals and is released from all sins.
Understanding, knowledge, clear thinking, patience, truth, self-control and calm; pleasure and pain, birth and death, fear and also fearlessness;
non-violence, even-mindedness, contentment, self-discipline, giving, fame and shame: all these different states of beings come from me alone.
The seven great sages of old and the four Manus were born from my mind and share my nature. All the creatures in the world come from them.

first: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
en: Whoever truly knows this glory and this power of mine is joined to me in steady yoga. There is no doubt about this.

first: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते ।
en: I am the origin of everything; everything moves forward from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with deep feeling.
With their minds on me and their lives given to me, they teach one another and always speak of me. In this they find contentment and joy.
To those who are always devoted and worship me with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to me.
Out of compassion for them, I, living in their hearts, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.

first: परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् ।
en: Arjuna said: You are the supreme Brahman, the highest home, the purest of all. You are the eternal, divine Person, the first God, unborn and all-pervading.
All the sages say this of you, and so do the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa. Now you yourself are telling me.
I accept as true everything you tell me, Keshava. Lord, neither the gods nor the demons know your real form.
You alone know yourself through yourself, highest Person, source and Lord of beings, God of gods, master of the world.
Please tell me fully of your divine glories, the powers through which you fill these worlds and remain in them.
How may I know you, master of yoga, as I keep thinking of you? In which forms, Lord, should I think of you?
Tell me again in detail about your power and your glory, Janardana. I never have enough of hearing your words; they are like nectar to me.
Krishna said: Very well, I will tell you of my divine glories, best of the Kurus, but only the main ones, for there is no end to my greatness.
Arjuna, I am the Self that lives in the heart of every being. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.
Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among lights I am the shining sun. Among the Maruts I am Marichi; among the stars I am the moon.
Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; among the gods I am Indra. Among the senses I am the mind; in living beings I am awareness.
Among the Rudras I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas I am Kubera, lord of wealth. Among the Vasus I am fire; among mountain peaks I am Meru.

first: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् ।
en: Know me, Partha, as Brihaspati, the chief of priests. Among army leaders I am Skanda; among bodies of water I am the ocean.
Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the single syllable Om. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of quiet repetition; among things that do not move I am the Himalaya.
Among all trees I am the sacred fig; among divine sages I am Narada. Among the Gandharvas I am Chitraratha; among the perfected ones I am the sage Kapila.
Among horses know me as Uchchaihshravas, born from the nectar; among great elephants, Airavata; and among men, the king.
Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am Kamadhenu, the cow that grants wishes. I am Kandarpa, the god of love who brings birth; among serpents I am Vasuki.
Among the Nagas I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among the ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who control I am Yama.
Among the Daityas I am Prahlada; among those who count I am Time. Among animals I am the lion; among birds I am Garuda.
Among purifiers I am the wind; among those who bear weapons I am Rama. Among fish I am the makara; among rivers I am the Ganga.
Of all creations I am the beginning, the end and also the middle, Arjuna. Among kinds of knowledge I am the knowledge of the Self; in those who debate I am the reasoning.
Among letters I am the letter A; among compound words I am the joining compound. I alone am endless Time; I am the giver who faces every direction.
I am death that takes everything, and the birth of all that is to come. Among feminine qualities I am fame, good fortune, speech, memory, wisdom, steadiness and patience.
Among the Sama hymns I am the Brihat Sama; among metres I am the Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring, the bringer of flowers.
Of cheats I am gambling; I am the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, I am effort, I am the goodness of the good.
Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa; among poets I am the poet Ushana.
Of those who punish I am the rod; of those who seek victory I am wise policy. Of secrets I am silence; of the wise I am wisdom.
Arjuna, whatever is the seed of all beings, that I am. Nothing, moving or unmoving, can exist without me.
There is no end to my divine glories, Parantapa. What I have told you is only a short sample of their range.
Whatever is glorious, beautiful or mighty, know that it has come from just a spark of my splendour.
But what use is all this detail to you, Arjuna? I hold up this whole universe with a single small part of myself.
